# Document models

A document model is a `powerhouse/document-model` document in the Vetra drive (`vetra-<hash>`). Codegen writes `document-models/<name>/v<n>/` from it, where `<name>` is the kebab-cased model name. Define the model through `reactor-mcp`, then implement reducers and tests in the generated folders. Never write `gen/` by hand.

## Plan

In an interactive session, present the proposal and wait for approval before creating anything. Without a user, state the proposal and continue.

The proposal names:

- Type id: `<organization>/<document-type-name>`, e.g. `pizza-plaza/order`, `acme/invoice`.
- Extension: 2 to 4 characters with a leading dot, e.g. `.ordr`, `.inv`.
- Name: matches `/[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9 ]*/`, human-readable and capitalized, e.g. `"Order"`, `"Invoice"`. Spaces drop out of code names: `"Book List"` gives the folder `book-list` and the state type `BookListState`.
- The state schema, global and, if needed, local. See [references/graphql-schema.md](references/graphql-schema.md).
- Modules, each with its operations, their input types and their errors.

Ask when the requirements are unclear. Split a complex model into modules of related operations.

### Design rules

- `global` scope: state shared among everyone with access to the document. `local` scope: state private to each user.
- One operation per user intent. Name operations for the intent, e.g. `ADD_LINE_ITEM`, `UPDATE_RECIPIENT`.
- Give every operation examples and error definitions.
- Group related operations into a module.

## Create a document model

1. Call `getDocumentModelSchema` with `type: "powerhouse/document-model"`. Read the input schema of every action you will send, so each call carries its required fields (`id`, `moduleId`, `operationId`, `scope`).
2. `createDocument` with `documentType: "powerhouse/document-model"` and `driveId` set to the `vetra-<hash>` drive.
3. Send the definition in as few `addActions` calls as possible (scope `global`):
   - Header: `SET_MODEL_NAME`, `SET_MODEL_ID` (the type id), `SET_MODEL_EXTENSION`, `SET_MODEL_DESCRIPTION`, `SET_AUTHOR_NAME`, `SET_AUTHOR_WEBSITE`.
   - State: `SET_STATE_SCHEMA` and `SET_INITIAL_STATE`, each with its `scope`.
   - Per module: `ADD_MODULE` (`{ id, name }`), then per operation `ADD_OPERATION` (`{ moduleId, id, name, schema, reducer }`), `SET_OPERATION_SCOPE` for a `local` operation, and `ADD_OPERATION_ERROR` per error.
   - The `id` fields of modules, operations and errors are ids inside the model; you choose them. Only document ids come from `createDocument`.
4. Codegen runs once the model is valid: it has an id and a name, at least one module, at least one operation per module, and an initial state for every state schema that defines fields. The global state type must be `<ModelName>State` and the local one `<ModelName>LocalState`; codegen refuses other names. Call `getCodegenStatus` with the model's `documentId` and `waitSeconds: 60`, and continue once it is `done`; `failed` or `skipped` carries the reason.
5. Implement each reducer in `v<n>/src/reducers/<module>.ts`. See [references/reducers.md](references/reducers.md).
6. Write tests in `v<n>/tests/` and run the checks. See [references/testing.md](references/testing.md).

## Change a document model

Change it in both places, every time:

1. Through `reactor-mcp`: `SET_STATE_SCHEMA`, `SET_OPERATION_SCHEMA`, `SET_OPERATION_REDUCER` and the other operations the schema lists. Skip this and the model keeps the old code: codegen writes a reducer from the model whenever `v<n>/src/reducers/` lacks it, which brings the old behaviour back.
2. In `v<n>/src/reducers/`. Skip this and the running code keeps the old behaviour: codegen never overwrites a reducer that already exists there.

After a state schema change, check every reducer that reads or writes the changed fields.

Call `getDocumentModelSchema` for the full list of document-model operations and their inputs. Two need a note:

- `RELEASE_NEW_VERSION` (input `{}`) starts version n+1 as a copy of the latest spec. Later changes apply to the new version.
- `ADD_OPERATION` takes an optional `scope` (default `global`). `SET_OPERATION_SCOPE` changes it later.

## What codegen writes

| Path | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| `document-models/<name>/v<n>/gen/` | Codegen. Never edit; it is overwritten. |
| `v<n>/src/reducers/<module>.ts` | You. Codegen adds a method for each operation the file lacks, from the model's reducer code or a stub that throws, and adds imports for the module's errors. It leaves existing methods alone. |
| `v<n>/tests/<module>.test.ts` | You. Codegen adds a `should handle <operation> operation` test, inside `describe("<Module>Operations")`, only for an operation the file doesn't test yet: no test of that name, no call of its action creator, no `"<OPERATION>"` string. |
| `v<n>/hooks.ts`, `actions.ts`, `utils.ts` | Codegen. Imported through the barrel. |
| `document-models/<name>` | The barrel. It points at the latest version. Import types, `actions`, hooks and `utils` from it. |

A new version starts with copies of the previous version's reducers and tests.

The model document holds:

- Metadata: `id`, `name`, `extension`, `description`, `author` (name and website).
- Specifications, one per version: `version`, `changeLog`, and `state` (global and local, each with schema, initial value and examples).
- Modules, each holding its operations.

## Check your work

- `npm run tsc`
- `npm run lint:fix`
- `npm run test:coverage` after a reducer change. Reducers stay at 95% or more on lines, branches, functions and statements.
